instructions: Bring a small pot of water to a boil with 1/2 tsp salt in it. Set a bowl of ice water next to the stove.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then transfer them to a large bowl. Mash them with a fork until about half are broken up and the rest are still whole.

Add the tahini, mustard, 1 grated garlic clove, capers, 2 chopped green onions, 1/4 cup chopped cilantro, 1/4 cup lemon juice from the lemons, 1/4 tsp salt and a few grinds of pepper. Stir until it holds together in a chunky scoop. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Trim the green beans and boil them for 1 1/2 minutes, until they're bright green. Transfer them to the ice water, then drain and pat dry. Cut them into 1-inch pieces.
Thinly slice the red onion, rinse the slices under cold water and pat them dry. Slice the cucumber half and the radishes into thin rounds.
Split the baguettes lengthwise. Spread the chickpea salad over the bottom halves and press the green beans into it. Top with the olives and red onion.
Spread the mayonnaise over the top halves. Layer on the cucumber, radishes and basil, then add a pinch of salt and pepper.
Press the halves together and cut each baguette in half so you have 4 sandwiches.
To pack, keep the chickpea salad in a covered container in the fridge for up to 3 days and build the sandwiches the morning you eat them.
method_notes: Love and Lemons mashes chickpeas with tahini, Dijon, capers and lemon, then builds the sandwich in layers like a pan bagnat with green beans, olives and basil, and that is the version used here. Other chickpea salad sandwiches bind the chickpeas with mayo, yogurt or avocado and add celery and dill. The tahini and capers keep this one dairy-free and well seasoned without a creamy binder. The filling keeps for days in the fridge, so the bread goes on last.
